caption: A lit sparkler stands upright in a cake, throwing off a spray of bright sparks that fade as they fall.

sa.check: A lit sparkler stands upright in a cake.
Sparks spray out from the sparkler's burning point.
The sparks fade as they travel.
The sparks travel away from the sparkler.

pc.expect: The sparks fly outward from the burning point and their paths bend downward, going dark before or as they land.
pc.fail: The sparks rise steadily and gather above the sparkler; or hang in the air; or lie on the cake glowing like lamps for the rest of the clip; or curve upward after leaving the wire.

pc.expect: Each spark fades within a short flight and none accumulate, and the sparkler is one wire.
pc.fail: Sparks persist as fixed bright dots; or a glowing pile builds on the cake; or sparks appear in the air far from the sparkler; or a second sparkler appears already lit.

pc.expect: The burning point only travels down the wire and the spent wire above it stays dark.
pc.fail: The burning point climbs back up the wire; or a dark part of the wire lights up again; or the burning point jumps to a new place on the wire; or the spent wire turns back to fresh coating.

pc.expect: The sparks come from the burning point and the wire behind it is spent.
pc.fail: The sparks come from a part of the wire that is still coated and unburnt; or the sparks come from the wire's tip while the burning point is elsewhere; or the sparkler burns with no sparks leaving it at all.

pc.expect: One sparkler in one cake; the wire stays a straight wire and the cake keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The wire bends into another shape; or the sparkler passes through the cake and out below; or a second wire appears; or the cake changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The cake's icing away from the sparkler, the plate and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The icing changes colour; or the plate changes pattern; or items on the table rearrange.
